# Pārivāsikakkhandhaka (Kd 12)
**ID:** Kd 12
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Pārivāsikakkhandhaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd12
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pārivāsikakkhandhaka* is the twelfth chapter of the Khandhaka section of the Vinaya Piṭaka, located in the *Cullavagga* immediately after the *Kammakkhandhaka* and before the *Samuccayakkhandhaka* [Norman 1983; Frauwallner 1956; Banerjee 1979]. It contains a detailed treatment of the conduct and duties required of a monastic who has committed an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*), outlining the standards of behavior to be observed while undergoing probation (*parivāsa*) in order to qualify for rehabilitation, as well as the conditions under which probation may temporarily be kept under suspension [SuttaCentral; Banerjee 1979]. In English, the chapter has been translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Pudgalavastu* in Sanskrit and *Parivāsa* in Tibetan and Chinese translations, along with the *Parivāsa Khandhaka* of the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka Vinayas, and resembling sections in the Mahāsaṅghika Vinaya and other Pali Khandhakas [SuttaCentral]. In comparative analysis, A. C. Banerjee notes that the Tibetan version largely corresponds with the Pali concerning the duties of a monk on probation and the suspension of probation, though unlike the Pali version it opens with an introductory narrative [Banerjee 1979]. DharmaNexus computational alignments show cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Pārivāsikavastu* and Tibetan Vinaya collections (including the *Vinayakṣudraka-vastu*, *Vinaya-uttaragrantha*, and *Vinayavibhaṅga*) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse across other Khandhaka chapters—such as the *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* (Kd 4), *Uposathakkhandhaka* (Kd 2), and *Kammakkhandhaka* (Kd 11)—as well as Vinaya subcommentaries including the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
